_what: Stage 27 diagnostics: can the loop learn the task by itself (cortical rule off)? 60-trial probes on network 31, cue -> striatum plastic, dopamine system on. Weights are cue-specific means per channel relative to their start.

probes.reading: common mode dominates: cue A depressed both channels' D1 x0.35-0.4 (A trials were mostly wrong), cue B potentiated both; the channel difference is 10-15 %
weights barely move; both SNr channels low during cues (shared cue drive)
right direction (A->ch1 > A->ch2 by 17 %, B->ch2 > B->ch1 by 23 %) but slow; D2 never fires so the NoGo side does not learn
thalamostriatal input closes a positive loop: both channels selected permanently, weights saturate
same lock, weights swing the other way

dopamine_in_all_probes: burst to reward 25-28 spikes/s (delta +1.1), pause to <0.3 spikes/s on error (delta -0.85 to -0.9); the critic stays near 0 because the mean reward is near 0 while accuracy is at chance
conclusion: the loop's synapses learn in the right direction but cannot assign credit between channels on their own: the cue drives both channels' striatum and the channel-specific signal (which pool won) is weak in this learner, whose two pools sit in one column with no cortical competition between them. The 150-trial loop-only runs (plastic_dl_*, two networks) confirm it: 40-55 % at trial 120.
